content.comment_body: Hello everyone, we are facing an issue with the [product_name] [article_no]. After finishing production, we often turn off the power. I'm unsure if this has caused any negative effects but today I noticed that on power up, it was in program mode.
Good afternoon [user_name], can you clarify what you mean by seeing it in program mode? Do you mean that instead of the normal main screen, it goes directly to the menu screen?
Does it always stay in program mode every time you power it off and on?

Are you saying the [product_name] should stop running its program after a power off event? In my experience, if I turn off the [product_name] while it's running and then power it on, it resumes in running mode. If it was stopped before power off, it starts up in stop mode. What is the situation with your [product_name]? Hope this helps.

A [product_name] running when power goes down will stop. When power is restored: if there is a memory module present, the program and settings from the memory module are loaded and the device starts running. If there is no memory module, it starts running with the internal program. You shouldn't lose the program due to a power outage. Note, if power is gone for a long time, the clock may be wrong. All settings with RETENTIVITY ON keep their value from before the power loss; those with RETENTIVITY OFF reset to their original value. The Hours Counter is always retained. The Marker M8 in certain models gives a single pulse on initial power-up cycle. The program is stored in FLASH memory and won't be lost unless manually deleted, lasting for many years.

If I understand correctly, the expectation is that the [product_name] should return to RUN mode automatically after power is restored, but it instead goes to programming mode. I haven't heard of this issue before. If no program is present, it would remain in STOP and couldn't be started, so that can't be the case here.

Hi everyone, I'm not exactly sure what happened. We restarted production after a few days of downtime, and suddenly the [product_name] wasn't producing any outputs. My colleague checked but found no changes. That morning, I connected my PC and uploaded the program. Later that day I returned and saw it in stop mode, as shown in the attached file. Then, I started it using the software and it worked correctly.
The picture provided is incomplete and doesn't help clarify the problem.

The [product_name] will show output when your program conditions are met with proper logic, so check your logic inputs, outputs, timers, etc. You can use online diagnostics to troubleshoot. If you need further help, please describe your problem in detail and provide error images.
How many times have you manually stopped and started the [product_name]?
This image was taken from the manual, but it matches the actual condition. In this scenario, the [product_name] is operating in user mode.
It only happened that one time. I'll check again if it occurs in the future.

The picture isn't complete, so it's not possible to see the full information. If you just want to confirm that the [product_name] displays the first entry in the system menu when there is a failure, then you don't need a picture. I am not aware of any error where the [product_name] with a running program is powered off and then fails to automatically resume RUN mode, starting at the system menu instead.

I've set my [product_name] to operator mode. After setting the display to show the menu screen on power-on, loading the program, switching off power, waiting five minutes, and turning it on again, I get the result shown in the picture. However, my [product_name] goes into run mode as expected.

I've set my [product_name] to operator mode, with the display showing the menu screen after power on. After loading the program, switching off power, waiting five minutes, and turning it on, my [product_name] enters run mode. That's the normal behavior as stated before; make sure there are no reset buttons affecting operations if it's not running.

As mentioned previously: First, your [product_name] must have a working program (it can be simple, like I1 equals Q1). Switch the [product_name] to RUN. If you don't use Text Blocks, you'll see the date and time on the display. If you turn power off and then on, the [product_name] always starts in RUN mode, whether the downtime is seconds or years. It only won't start in RUN automatically if it was not running when powered off, even if the program is intact.
Has your issue been resolved, [user_name]?
Have you checked your logic inputs? The high output depends on the input conditions being met. You should understand your logic operation and how it works.

You can easily check inputs, outputs, and other conditions on the [product_name]. When date and time appear on the display and it's in RUN status, pressing the left or right cursor key will show actual inputs, outputs, analog values, and markers. This is helpful for diagnosing issues if the [product_name] isn't working as expected.
Thank you. This issue has only occurred once so far.
The problem happened while I wasn't present. The next day, I followed your advice and checked as you suggested.
A new question published by [user_name] has been moved to a separate thread regarding [product_name] entering STOP mode. Best regards [user_name]
There is a setting to choose what the display shows after power on. I believe it's currently set to menu. Adjust it to display the time and date.

analysis.insight_summary: Users described unexpected behavior from the [product_name] [article_no] after restoring power, where the device did not automatically resume RUN mode and outputs did not activate as expected. There is uncertainty around whether the device should retain its previous operational state or require manual intervention after a power cycle. Lack of clarity on retentivity and recovery undermines user confidence in system reliability.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [product_name] [article_no] to reliably return to its previous RUN state and resume outputs after power is restored, without the need for manual reconfiguration or reloading the program.
